PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Explicit distributed failure, timing, network, storage and recovery model
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Byzantine agreement (1982), asynchronous impossibility (1985), partial synchrony (1988) and failure-detector theory (1996).
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: State the process, communication, clock and storage faults an algorithm tolerates and the timing assumptions under which it progresses.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Protocol names are often repeated after the assumptions that make their guarantees true have been dropped.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Crash, omission, delay, partition, corruption, clock and recovery faults are conflated; a proved algorithm is deployed outside its model.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Invalid inference from algorithm identity to deployed safety, liveness, consistency or recoverability.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Attach every guarantee to an explicit model; check implementation primitives, failure domains and recovery transitions against it.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any correctness or completion claim spanning independently failing processes, stores, networks or administrative components.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A local call, local transaction or one durable process when no independent remote failure boundary is required.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Known component boundary; declared synchrony; stable-storage semantics; restart behaviour; membership; clock assumptions; common-mode inventory.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Crash-stop, crash-recovery, omission, delay, partition, storage corruption, clock error and correlated/common-mode failure as applicable.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: The claim states whether it is asynchronous, partially synchronous, synchronous, or merely bounded by a local policy timeout.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: No consistency claim is accepted without a named history/observation model and operation boundary.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Membership, configuration and ownership identity are explicit wherever they affect the claim.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Loss, duplication, reordering and retry are either in scope or explicitly excluded.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Restart, stable-storage, rollback and rejoin semantics are declared.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Evidence distinguishes suspicion from established failure and reports coverage gaps.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents model-free folklore, focuses tests on the actual fault envelope and makes evidence comparable.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, protocol implementer, operator, reviewer and consumer of a distributed guarantee.
KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Recovery changes membership outside the proof
Implementation primitive is weaker than the model
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Enumerating assumptions is not proof they hold
Byzantine language can distract from ordinary crash/common-mode failures
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From generic 'node failure' to layered profiles covering process, network, clock, storage, restart, configuration, operator and common-mode coupling.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: An assumption contract travels with each guarantee, test and recovery path, and names the local cheap path.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Using a protocol or topology label is ceremony; the retained property is the checked model.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should correlated operator/control-plane faults be represented without making the model intractable?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What exact crash, restart, storage, timing, network and common-mode failures are in scope?
Which claims fail if a timeout is a false suspicion or storage returns corrupted—not merely absent—data?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Partial failure and unknown-outcome semantics
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: RPC retransmission and end-to-end semantics, failure detectors and later retry/reconciliation practice.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: A missing response means the caller lacks evidence about remote execution; it does not prove nonexecution.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: One component can continue or commit while another is slow, paused, partitioned, restarted or unable to receive the reply.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: The caller times out after the remote effect may already have committed or may still be executing.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Timeout-triggered duplicate action, abandoned committed work or unsafe failover.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Represent UNKNOWN/PENDING outcomes; query by stable operation identity; reconcile, retry safely or compensate; propagate deadlines separately.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Remote mutation, distributed commit, task dispatch or external side effect whose response can be lost.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Local atomic mutation with a definitive return, or a harmless repeatable read.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable operation identity, authoritative status/reconciliation interface, durable outcome state and duplicate-safe or compensatable effect.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Crash-stop, crash-recovery, omission, delay, partition, storage corruption, clock error and correlated/common-mode failure as applicable.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: The claim states whether it is asynchronous, partially synchronous, synchronous, or merely bounded by a local policy timeout.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: No consistency claim is accepted without a named history/observation model and operation boundary.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Membership, configuration and ownership identity are explicit wherever they affect the claim.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Loss, duplication, reordering and retry are either in scope or explicitly excluded.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Restart, stable-storage, rollback and rejoin semantics are declared.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Evidence distinguishes suspicion from established failure and reports coverage gaps.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Makes epistemic uncertainty explicit and prevents timeout from becoming a false semantic verdict.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Caller, orchestrator, operator and business decision deciding whether to retry, wait or compensate.
KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Retry races the original slow execution
Cancellation stops waiting but not work
Status record is lost with worker
Operation identity reused for changed parameters
Unknown is prematurely mapped to failed
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Unknown-state handling adds latency and durable state
Some external effects cannot be queried or reversed
Aggressive timeouts can create the uncertainty they detect
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From RPC retry rules to durable unknown states, semantic operation identity, deadline propagation and reconciliation.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Timeout/no response yields UNKNOWN until authoritative postcondition, idempotent closure or compensation resolves it.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Turning timeout into an error code is not the property.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How long may an outcome remain unknown before policy must escalate or compensate?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: When a timeout expires, can the target still commit or act?
Where is UNKNOWN represented, and what authoritative observation resolves it?
Can cancellation prevent the old actor from acting?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Failure-domain independence and common-mode awareness
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Primary/backup and quorum replication, refined by geo-distributed placement and field studies of correlated failure.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Place redundant state and decision paths across failure domains independent for the failures being claimed.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Replicas share power, network, storage software, configuration, control plane, credentials, operator or region.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: A common cause removes or corrupts nominally redundant copies and the recovery/control path.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Replica count being mistaken for independent availability or durability coverage.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Map physical and logical shared fate; place replicas/witnesses/control paths accordingly; bound corruption propagation and test correlated failure.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Replication, quorum, backup, multi-zone/region, control-plane or failover claim.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: One durable copy plus tested backup where hot availability is unnecessary and consequence permits it.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Failure-domain inventory, placement evidence, recovery-path independence, integrity checks and out-of-band access.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Crash-stop, crash-recovery, omission, delay, partition, storage corruption, clock error and correlated/common-mode failure as applicable.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: The claim states whether it is asynchronous, partially synchronous, synchronous, or merely bounded by a local policy timeout.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: No consistency claim is accepted without a named history/observation model and operation boundary.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Membership, configuration and ownership identity are explicit wherever they affect the claim.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Loss, duplication, reordering and retry are either in scope or explicitly excluded.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Restart, stable-storage, rollback and rejoin semantics are declared.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Evidence distinguishes suspicion from established failure and reports coverage gaps.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Turns 'N replicas' into a defensible fault-coverage claim and reveals shared recovery dependencies.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Storage/platform owner, resilience architect, incident commander and recovery planner.
KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Recovery credentials/DNS depend on failed system
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Cross-region independence costs latency and complexity
Provider labels are not empirical proof
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From hardware redundancy to multi-layer common-mode analysis including software, configuration, control and operator.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Claim tolerance only for explicit independent domains; include data, authority, observability and recovery paths.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Three replicas or three zones is ceremony without a shared-fate model.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can tenants independently verify cloud failure-domain claims?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Which replicas share software, configuration, network, storage, credentials, DNS, control plane or operator?
Can anti-entropy, repair or global configuration spread one bad state everywhere?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Causal order distinguished from wall-clock and arbitrary total order
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Lamport's happens-before relation (1978), vector clocks, causal multicast and causal consistency.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Represent causal precedence and concurrency without assuming a perfect global clock.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Wall-clock skew, log merge order or arbitrary tie-breaking reverses or invents dependencies.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Events are delayed, reordered and concurrent across independently progressing processes.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Conflict resolution, replay, audit or a decision using an order that does not preserve the relation it needs.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Use logical/vector/dependency clocks, causal delivery or a deliberately authoritative sequencer; preserve concurrency instead of fabricating a winner.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Correctness depends on whether one event could have influenced another, read-your-writes or dependency application.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Single-thread/local transaction order, or independent commutative operations with no causal consumer.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable event identity, propagation of dependency metadata, stated sequencer/log semantics and retention of causal context.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Delay, reordering, concurrency, partition, clock skew/jumps, replica lag and incomplete propagation.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: No exact global clock is assumed unless a measured uncertainty bound and failure response are part of the design.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Causal, session, linearizable, snapshot or bounded-staleness semantics are named per operation.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Sequencers, leases and readers identify the current term/configuration where that affects currentness.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Event identity and dependency metadata survive retry/replay; transport order is not promoted to causal order.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Replay and failover preserve required dependencies and do not present older state as newer without signalling.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Clock uncertainty, lag, missing dependencies and sampled evidence remain visible.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents false temporal inference and enables safe concurrency where total coordination is unnecessary.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Database designer, event processor, workflow author, auditor and debugger.
KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Dependency metadata dropped at a boundary
Log order mistaken for real-world causality
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Causality does not supply semantic conflict resolution
Some invariants genuinely require total order
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From wall-clock/process-local sequence to explicit partial order, causal/session guarantees and hybrid logical time.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Choose the weakest order that protects the consumer; name causal, sequencer/log, commit, event-time and observation-time separately.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Adding a timestamp or correlation ID is not causal engineering.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can causal metadata be bounded without silently losing dependencies?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Where does the system rely on wall-clock or log order, and does that order preserve the needed causal relation?
Can concurrent events remain concurrent, or are they silently collapsed by last-write-wins?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Bounded-clock use and time-based authority with uncertainty margin
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Clock-synchronisation bounds, leases and systems using bounded time uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Use physical time only with a declared uncertainty/drift model; never infer exact global order or current authority from local time alone.

PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Stale owners mutating after handoff, premature TTL/dedup expiry and false timestamp order.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Use monotonic clocks for durations, uncertainty intervals for ordering, conservative expiry, and resource-enforced generations/fencing.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Leases, TTLs, freshness SLAs, event-time windows or external-consistency designs.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Logical/causal clocks, non-time-based generations, or local timeout used only as a heuristic.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Measured bound, uncertainty excursion policy, pause/restart handling, lease issuer identity and fenced effect boundary.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Delay, reordering, concurrency, partition, clock skew/jumps, replica lag and incomplete propagation.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: No exact global clock is assumed unless a measured uncertainty bound and failure response are part of the design.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Causal, session, linearizable, snapshot or bounded-staleness semantics are named per operation.

PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Replay and failover preserve required dependencies and do not present older state as newer without signalling.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Clock uncertainty, lag, missing dependencies and sampled evidence remain visible.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Allows low-latency time-based mechanisms while retaining explicit safety margins.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Database, lock/lease service, scheduler, cache and operator.

TTL treated as proof of nonexecution

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Consistency level and isolation as an operation-scoped contract
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Serialisability and concurrency-control theory, linearizability, isolation critique, CAP/PACELC, causal and highly available transactions.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Name the history property, operation boundary and failure behaviour instead of saying 'strong', 'ACID' or 'eventual'.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Different models prevent different anomalies and impose different latency, availability and coordination costs.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Concurrent operations and replicas produce histories whose anomalies are hidden by vague labels.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Application invariants being assumed protected by a weaker model, or stronger semantics bought without a consumer.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Derive the model from invariants and observations; document permitted anomalies; test histories and failure cases.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Shared mutable state with concurrent actors or replicas.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Single-thread/local immutable data, or commutative/invariant-confluent operations tolerating declared anomalies.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Operation/transaction boundaries, anomaly model, client/session semantics, implementation verification and failure response.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Replica divergence, stale reads, concurrent writes, partition, corruption, repair error, common-mode failure and obsolete membership.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Availability and convergence may be asynchronous; bounded staleness requires a separate bound and measurement.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: The replica model, permitted anomalies, convergence rule and semantic invariant are explicit.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Replica set, writer authority and configuration identity are current and durable.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Replication messages tolerate duplicate/reorder according to the protocol and retain required version metadata.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Catch-up, repair, rejoin, compaction and corruption handling are tested.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Lag, divergence, repair source, membership and invariant checks are observable.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Aligns coordination cost with the invariant and blocks consistency-by-brand.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Application/data designer, database owner, reviewer and consumer.
KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: External effect not covered by DB consistency
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Formal labels are hard to apply
Stronger consistency can reduce availability without protecting a real invariant
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From ACID/BASE slogans to named per-operation models, session guarantees, invariant-based selection and anomaly checks.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Each operation states required history semantics, protected invariant and failure response; stronger coordination is localised.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Selecting a product tier labelled 'strong' is ceremony.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should application invariants be translated into checkable consistency obligations across systems?

PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Offline, geo or multi-writer state where concurrent progress is valuable.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: One current writer, local transaction or coordination when the invariant is non-confluent.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Operation algebra, identity/tombstone policy, causal metadata, invariant argument and compaction horizon.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Replica divergence, stale reads, concurrent writes, partition, corruption, repair error, common-mode failure and obsolete membership.

PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Replica set, writer authority and configuration identity are current and durable.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Quorum validity bound to current membership and configuration
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Weighted voting, Paxos-family quorums, consensus and strongly consistent databases.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: An intersecting decision set is meaningful only relative to the same legitimate configuration and state/version.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A numeric majority forms from the wrong, stale, duplicated or non-independent member set.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Partitions and reconfiguration allow conflicting views of who may vote or serve state.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Two configurations each forming majority, stale state winning or restored identity voting twice.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Version membership; bind votes to term/configuration/log position; preserve intersection through reconfiguration; validate durable identities and placement.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Replicated decision, leader election, lock service or strong database read/write.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: One current durable owner or local transaction.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Authoritative configuration identity, unique durable member ID, persisted vote/log and proven transitional overlap.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Crash-recovery, network partition, delayed/stale messages, duplicated identity, reconfiguration and—only when declared—arbitrary faults.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Safety and liveness assumptions are separated; progress usually relies on partial synchrony and a reachable quorum.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Agreement/order does not itself establish application semantic validity.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Terms, views, ballots, configurations and durable member identity bind every decision and mutation.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Protocol messages are term/configuration bound and stale messages are rejected.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Votes, log position, snapshots and configuration state survive restart without rollback of authority.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Current term, configuration, quorum and commit position can be reconstructed.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents majority folklore from masking split authority.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Consensus/database implementer, operator and failover controller.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Larger quorums reduce availability and raise latency
Intersection does not validate application values
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From static vote counts to configuration-indexed quorum certificates and safe reconfiguration.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A quorum certificate identifies current configuration, epoch and state position.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: 'Three nodes, therefore safe' is ceremony.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should decommissioned identities be prevented from reappearing after restore?

PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A protocol remains safe but unavailable, or all replicas agree on a syntactically valid yet semantically wrong value.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Partitions, slow links and failures prevent progress while agreement remains intact; agreement can choose bad input.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Unsafe manual fail-open, false continuous-availability claim or consensus-as-business-oracle.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: State safety invariant, liveness assumptions and input/application validity separately; expose quorum loss rather than violating safety.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Replicated exclusive decision or ordered log whose divergence would violate an invariant.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Local durable owner, commutative/partitionable state or explicit manual arbitration.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Fault/timing model, durable vote/log, membership, deterministic application and input validation.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Crash-recovery, network partition, delayed/stale messages, duplicated identity, reconfiguration and—only when declared—arbitrary faults.

PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Votes, log position, snapshots and configuration state survive restart without rollback of authority.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Current term, configuration, quorum and commit position can be reconstructed.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Provides replicated decisions without pretending to guarantee continuous availability or semantic correctness.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Protocol implementer, state-machine validator and operator.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Single-writer or local-transaction cheap path

PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Distribution is introduced without a scale, latency, autonomy or availability consumer.

PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: This property is the cheap path; distribution triggers only after a concrete consumer appears.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Clear ownership, local durability, tested backup and fenced promotion if automatic failover exists.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Replica divergence, stale reads, concurrent writes, partition, corruption, repair error, common-mode failure and obsolete membership.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Availability and convergence may be asynchronous; bounded staleness requires a separate bound and measurement.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: The replica model, permitted anomalies, convergence rule and semantic invariant are explicit.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Replica set, writer authority and configuration identity are current and durable.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Replication messages tolerate duplicate/reorder according to the protocol and retain required version metadata.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Catch-up, repair, rejoin, compaction and corruption handling are tested.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Lag, divergence, repair source, membership and invariant checks are observable.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces state space, remote unknown outcomes and operational burden.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect and application/data owner.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: One process is not automatically durable
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From primary-copy replication to an explicit design-first cheap path.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Start local or single-writer; distribute only the dimension with demonstrated need.

PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Distributed serialisability, atomic commit, consensus and invariant-confluence analysis.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Coordinate operations whose independent execution can jointly violate a named invariant.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Locally valid concurrent decisions violate global uniqueness, conservation, bounds or exclusive ownership.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Partitioned or concurrent actors each act on incomplete state and jointly break the invariant.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Double allocation, oversell, duplicate uniqueness, inconsistent atomic transition or divergent ownership.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Use serialisable transaction, consensus, conditional write, reservation/escrow or authoritative sequencer over the minimal invariant boundary.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Demonstrated non-confluence, globally scarce resource or irreversible action requiring an exclusive current decision.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Independent commutative operations, ownership partitioning, escrowed budgets or one local owner.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Invariant definition, operation set, consistency target, current authority/membership, failure and recovery model.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Concurrent updates, coordinator/participant crash, partition, partial commit, blocked in-doubt state, duplicate side effect and failed compensation.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Blocking and latency under partition/long-running work are explicit; timeout does not resolve atomic outcome.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Atomicity/isolation covers only the declared transaction boundary; external effects need another closure.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Participants/coordinator/owners and transaction generation are durable and current.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Transaction messages and external calls have stable identity and duplicate-safe recovery.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Coordinator logs, participant states, compensation/forward-recovery ordering and manual resolution are durable.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Prepared/in-doubt/committed/compensating states and unresolved external effects are discoverable.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Preserves a real invariant while containing coordination cost.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Application/data owner and the consumer harmed by invariant violation.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Some invariants can be redesigned or escrowed
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From global transactions and locks to invariant-scoped coordination and hybrid strong/weak designs.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Demonstrate non-confluence, then coordinate the smallest state/effect closure or redesign the operation.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Consensus everywhere is ceremony; invariant-scoped coordination is the property.

PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Define maximum retry/replay/rejoin horizon; retain identity/tombstone/result evidence at least that long; reject or manually reconcile older arrivals.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Finite dedup cache, TTL, log retention, replay, delayed replica rejoin or disaster restore.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: No retries/replay and bounded local execution, or effect is naturally harmless under repetition.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: End-to-end maximum delay, restore age, retention policy, compaction rules and explicit post-expiry consequence.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.

PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Makes exactly-once/effect claims falsifiable in time instead of implicitly permanent.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Broker/storage owner, API owner, workflow and recovery planner.
KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Consumer offset retained less than data
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Unbounded partitions make finite guarantees impossible

PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Every dedup/compaction expiry has an explicit maximum-age assumption and behaviour for older arrivals.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A seven-day idempotency window is not a permanent exactly-once guarantee.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Acknowledgement separated from verified external effect
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: End-to-end arguments, RPC ambiguity, transaction commit records and workflow completion semantics.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: An ACK proves only the exact durable boundary that emitted it; it does not prove the intended downstream or real-world postcondition.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Callers treat receipt, queue acceptance, worker DONE or DB commit as proof the whole intended action occurred.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Effects cross several independent systems and some acknowledgements are lost or emitted before downstream completion.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: False completion, lost external action, duplicate retry and unreconciled partial effects.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Name ACK boundary; link it to operation identity; verify required external postcondition or atomically close/compensate the remaining boundary.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Multi-hop action, asynchronous processing, third-party/physical effect or workflow completion.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Single local transaction whose return covers the entire required state change.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Declared postcondition, authoritative observation, provenance, effect identity and uncertainty/compensation policy.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Makes completion meaningful to the consumer rather than transport-local.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Caller, orchestrator, business owner and incident responder.
KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Success cached while downstream rolled back
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Independent verification may be expensive or impossible
Some effects are only probabilistically observable
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From transport receipt to end-to-end effect evidence and explicit residual uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Completion is defined by the consumer's postcondition, with the evidence boundary and remaining uncertainty stated.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Transactional messaging or outbox/inbox closure
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Transaction logs, reliable messaging, stream-processing checkpoint/offset integration and outbox/inbox practice.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Close the atomicity gap between local state change and message publication/consumption.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A service commits state but fails to publish, publishes but rolls back, or applies an effect and crashes before advancing acknowledgement.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Database and broker fail independently; network/retry separates commit from message acknowledgement.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Lost event, duplicate state transition, offset/effect skew and inconsistent downstream projection.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Atomically write state plus outbox, or transactionally commit broker records/offsets and local state; consumers use inbox/dedup and replay.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: A local transaction must reliably cause or record an asynchronous message, or a consumed event must update state exactly once within the closure.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Direct local state change with no asynchronous notification requirement.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable event identity, publisher relay/recovery, ordering assumptions, dedup horizon and explicit external-effect boundary.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Creates a recoverable handoff between local atomicity and asynchronous delivery.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Service owner, broker/stream operator, projection and workflow.
KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Event order differs from state order
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Still not atomic with arbitrary third parties
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From distributed transaction aspiration to bounded local transaction plus durable handoff and duplicate-safe consumption.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: The state-to-message boundary has a durable recovery record; any remaining external boundary is explicit.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Having a broker and an outbox table is not closure if relay, dedup and replay are unowned.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Explicit transactional boundary and atomic-commit choice
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Transactions, distributed serialisability, two-phase/nonblocking commit and later deterministic/geo transaction systems.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Identify exactly which participants and effects commit atomically, and the failure/blocking model of that choice.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Atomicity is assumed across databases, messages and external systems that are not in one commit protocol.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Coordinator or participant fails between prepare/commit; partitions leave in-doubt participants or partial external effects.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Partial commit, contradictory participant outcomes and false rollback expectations.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Use local transaction, 2PC/consensus-backed transaction, deterministic ordering or another atomic protocol only for participating resources; persist in-doubt state.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: A non-compensatable invariant requires all-or-nothing across multiple transactional participants.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: One local transaction; or independently commit compensatable steps with a durable saga.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Participant durability, coordinator log, isolation, recovery protocol, timeout semantics and explicit exclusion of nonparticipants.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Concurrent updates, coordinator/participant crash, partition, partial commit, blocked in-doubt state, duplicate side effect and failed compensation.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Blocking and latency under partition/long-running work are explicit; timeout does not resolve atomic outcome.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Atomicity/isolation covers only the declared transaction boundary; external effects need another closure.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Participants/coordinator/owners and transaction generation are durable and current.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Transaction messages and external calls have stable identity and duplicate-safe recovery.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Coordinator logs, participant states, compensation/forward-recovery ordering and manual resolution are durable.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Prepared/in-doubt/committed/compensating states and unresolved external effects are discoverable.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Makes atomicity real within a defensible boundary and exposes blocking/availability cost.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Database/application designer, coordinator and recovery operator.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Blanket rejection ignores cases where atomicity is worth cost
Blanket adoption extends scope too far
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From global transaction aspiration to scoped atomicity, replicated coordinators, deterministic ordering and hybrid saga boundaries.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Choose atomic commit for a named non-compensatable closure; otherwise prefer local transactions plus durable handoff/compensation.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: 'ACID' or '2PC' without participant/effect boundary is ceremony.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which modern workloads justify the latency/availability cost of cross-region atomic commit?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Which resources actually participate in one atomic commit?
What state remains in-doubt after coordinator or network failure, and how is it resolved?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Compensation and forward recovery with semantic limits
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Sagas and long-running transaction practice, later durable workflow systems.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Recover a long-running distributed operation through ordered compensating or forward actions when global rollback is unavailable.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Steps commit independently and some effects cannot be transactionally rolled back.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Later step fails after earlier durable/internal/external effects; compensation can also fail or be non-inverse.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Permanent unowned partial business state and false claim that rollback restores the past.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Persist saga state; define compensations/reservations/semantic locks; order and retry them safely; use forward recovery when reversal is impossible; escalate residuals.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Long-running, cross-service or external workflow whose effects are compensatable or repairable but not globally atomic.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: One atomic local/distributed transaction when the whole closure can and should commit together.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Effect identity, compensation semantics, ordering, duplicate safety, durable orchestration, current external-state observation and manual path.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Concurrent updates, coordinator/participant crash, partition, partial commit, blocked in-doubt state, duplicate side effect and failed compensation.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Blocking and latency under partition/long-running work are explicit; timeout does not resolve atomic outcome.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Atomicity/isolation covers only the declared transaction boundary; external effects need another closure.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Participants/coordinator/owners and transaction generation are durable and current.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Transaction messages and external calls have stable identity and duplicate-safe recovery.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Coordinator logs, participant states, compensation/forward-recovery ordering and manual resolution are durable.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Prepared/in-doubt/committed/compensating states and unresolved external effects are discoverable.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Provides a governed recovery path for partial effects without pretending compensation is a true inverse.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Workflow/business owner, service teams and operations.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Complexity may exceed a scoped transaction
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From named compensating transactions to durable, observable, idempotent compensation/forward-recovery plans with residual-state handling.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Compensation states what it restores, what it cannot restore and how unresolved residuals are detected and escalated.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A compensating endpoint on a diagram is not recovery evidence.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Durable workflow state as a recoverable distributed state machine
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Sagas, workflow systems, durable logs and modern serverless durable execution.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Persist enough workflow history/state that orchestration survives process loss and resumes deterministically or by explicit repair.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Request/worker memory is lost on restart; timers, child work, retries and compensation become orphaned.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Orchestrator and workers fail independently while tasks and external effects continue.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Lost long-running work, duplicate restart, forgotten timers/compensations and operator guesswork.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Persist workflow transitions/history, task identities, timers, signals and terminal state; replay or recover from snapshot/log; expose manual intervention.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Long-running, multi-step, retrying or externally signalled work that must survive process/platform restart.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Synchronous local call/transaction whose whole lifetime fits one reliable execution boundary.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Durable ordered history, stable workflow/run identity, deterministic/versioned orchestration and external-effect reconciliation.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Worker/orchestrator crash, task redelivery, lease expiry, orphaned work, replay, cancellation race, code-version change and external side-effect uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Timers, heartbeats and leases are policy evidence; they do not prove prior execution stopped.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Durable workflow state is distinct from correctness/currentness of external systems.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Workflow run, task attempt and worker generation identify current ownership; stale effects are fenced or neutralised.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Activity dispatch is assumed duplicable unless the entire effect boundary is atomically closed.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: History/snapshot replay, versioning, unknown-effect reconciliation and manual intervention are retained.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Workflow state, task attempts, effect status and version are reconstructable.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Makes distributed work state recoverable and inspectable rather than implicit in transient processes.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Workflow author, orchestration runtime, operator and business owner.
KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Terminal state set before effect verified
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Durability does not guarantee semantic correctness of external world
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From ad hoc retry scripts and sagas to durable state machines with history, timers, signals and explicit effect boundaries.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Workflow history is authoritative for orchestration, while external state is independently validated where required.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Deploying a workflow engine is not the property if workflow/effect state is not durable and reconcilable.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What workflow state survives orchestrator restart?
Can the durable history reconstruct task ownership, retries, timers, signals and unresolved external effects?

PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Workflow state, task attempts, effect status and version are reconstructable.

PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Orchestrator, scheduler, worker and effect owner.

New attempt uses new operation ID

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Bounded queues with explicit work-age and capacity semantics
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Queueing/service systems, staged event-driven architectures and production overload experience.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: A queue is finite deferred work against finite service capacity, not an infinite availability reservoir.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Acceptance continues after completion capacity is exhausted; backlog age and memory/storage grow until service or recovery collapses.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Producers and consumers scale/fail independently; queue hides demand from upstream while downstream saturates.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Unbounded memory/disk growth, extreme latency, expired work, recovery surge and hidden overload.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Bound depth/age/bytes; attach deadlines and priority; reject/shed/spill according to consequence policy; size from service rate and recovery capacity.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Asynchronous buffering between independently varying producer and consumer demand.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Direct synchronous flow with natural backpressure, or small fixed local buffer where overload consequence is acceptable.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Measured arrival/service distributions, deadline/value policy, storage limit, drain/recovery capacity and rejection semantics.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Queue growth, shared bottleneck saturation, retry amplification, synchronized clients, head-of-line blocking, cascading failure and metastable positive feedback.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Deadlines and service-time distributions matter; old work may be worthless even if capacity eventually returns.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Consequence policy defines which work may be rejected, degraded, delayed or shed.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Admission and priority policy has a defined owner; no implicit per-hop policy conflict.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Retries preserve operation identity and consume an explicit budget; shedding has visible consequence.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Backlog drain, retry release and recovery surge are capacity-bounded and observed.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Queue age/depth, utilization, demand, retry rate, deadlines, drop reasons and dependency saturation are visible.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Makes queueing a deliberate latency/capacity trade rather than overload concealment.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Service owner, queue/stream operator, capacity planner and business owner.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Capacity estimates vary and can be wrong
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From unbounded buffering to multidimensional limits on count, bytes, age and consequence, tied to drain/recovery tests.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Queue admission is governed by the probability and value of completing work before its deadline, with explicit shed/defer behaviour.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: 'We put a queue in front' is not resilience.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should shared queues preserve fairness and critical work under shifting demand?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Is queue capacity bounded by count, bytes and age, and by actual drain capacity?
What happens to work that cannot finish before its deadline?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Backpressure propagated to the source of demand
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Flow control, bounded-buffer systems, stream processing and service-overload control.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: A saturated consumer communicates a rate/credit/refusal signal upstream before queues and retries amplify demand.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Local queues fill while producers continue at an unconstrained rate; overload moves rather than resolves.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Each hop sees only local capacity and can amplify or buffer requests independently.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Cascading queue growth, wasted work, timeout storms and downstream collapse.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Credit/rate/window control, demand signalling, concurrency limits, propagated deadline/refusal, or producer throttling across the dependency graph.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Producer can outpace consumer or fan-out multiplies work.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: In-process bounded channel or naturally demand-driven iterator when no remote graph exists.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Current dependency topology, demand accounting, admission semantics, retry integration and fairness policy.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Queue growth, shared bottleneck saturation, retry amplification, synchronized clients, head-of-line blocking, cascading failure and metastable positive feedback.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Deadlines and service-time distributions matter; old work may be worthless even if capacity eventually returns.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Consequence policy defines which work may be rejected, degraded, delayed or shed.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Admission and priority policy has a defined owner; no implicit per-hop policy conflict.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Retries preserve operation identity and consume an explicit budget; shedding has visible consequence.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Backlog drain, retry release and recovery surge are capacity-bounded and observed.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Queue age/depth, utilization, demand, retry rate, deadlines, drop reasons and dependency saturation are visible.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Aligns offered load with bottleneck capacity and stops overload migration.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Producer, intermediary, downstream owner and platform traffic controller.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Backpressure can reduce utilisation or create unfairness
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From hop-local flow control to dependency-aware end-to-end demand propagation and adaptive limits.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Every admission path—including retries and async queues—consumes an explicit capacity signal that reaches demand origin.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A local queue watermark with unconstrained upstream retries is not backpressure.

PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Overload collapse, tail amplification, critical-work starvation and invisible business loss.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Concurrency/rate limits, priority and fairness, deadline-aware admission, graceful degradation and explicit rejection/deferral semantics.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Demand can exceed sustainable service or shared bottlenecks can saturate.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Fixed small system with hard external demand limit and no shared saturation risk.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Capacity model, criticality/value classes, fairness policy, caller-visible rejection semantics, retry budget and telemetry.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Queue growth, shared bottleneck saturation, retry amplification, synchronized clients, head-of-line blocking, cascading failure and metastable positive feedback.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Deadlines and service-time distributions matter; old work may be worthless even if capacity eventually returns.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Consequence policy defines which work may be rejected, degraded, delayed or shed.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Admission and priority policy has a defined owner; no implicit per-hop policy conflict.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Retries preserve operation identity and consume an explicit budget; shedding has visible consequence.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Backlog drain, retry release and recovery surge are capacity-bounded and observed.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Queue age/depth, utilization, demand, retry rate, deadlines, drop reasons and dependency saturation are visible.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Preserves useful work and system recoverability instead of maximising accepted-but-doomed work.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Traffic controller, service owner, product/business owner and clients.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Retry budgets, exponential backoff, jitter and deadline propagation
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: RPC retry practice, congestion/overload control and production guidance on coordinated retries.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Retries consume bounded capacity and time; they are not free availability.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Every layer retries independently, synchronously and after the operation's useful deadline.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Partial failures/timeouts cause many clients to retransmit into a degraded shared dependency.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Retry storms, duplicate effects, wasted work, thundering herd and deadline overrun.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Centralise/allocate retry budget; cap attempts; use exponential backoff with jitter; honour end-to-end deadline; retry only classified/transient/duplicate-safe operations.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Transient failure can plausibly recover within the remaining deadline and retry is semantically safe.

PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Low-utilisation local system with no feedback path and trivial restart.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Dependency graph, demand/capacity telemetry, feedback-loop hypothesis, safe shedding and tested recovery ramp.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Queue growth, shared bottleneck saturation, retry amplification, synchronized clients, head-of-line blocking, cascading failure and metastable positive feedback.

PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Consequence policy defines which work may be rejected, degraded, delayed or shed.

PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Retries preserve operation identity and consume an explicit budget; shedding has visible consequence.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Consistent distributed snapshot or checkpoint
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Chandy–Lamport snapshots, coordinated checkpointing and stream-processing snapshots.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Capture a recovery cut that is consistent with message/channel and state transitions, not an arbitrary set of local copies.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Independent checkpoints combine states that never coexisted; in-flight messages/effects are lost or duplicated.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Components checkpoint at different times while messages and transactions continue.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Impossible restored state, orphan messages, domino rollback and duplicate/lost processing.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Marker/barrier/coordinated checkpoint or equivalent protocol records local state plus required channel/log position; validate completeness and durability.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Recovery, migration, rescaling or audit requires a cross-component state cut.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: One local transactional snapshot or reconstructable stateless workers.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Declared channel/order assumptions, checkpoint metadata, atomic durable write, log position and compatible application state.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Process/storage crash, partition, inconsistent checkpoint, orphan message/work, log gap, corruption, stale failover authority and external-state divergence.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Recovery point/time objectives are evidence-backed, not inferred from backup existence.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: The recovery line is internally consistent and reconciled with effects outside the log/transaction boundary.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Restored configuration, ownership generation and membership are current; old writers are fenced.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Replay/redelivery uses original identities and does not duplicate unclosed effects.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Snapshots, logs, backups, restore tooling, capacity and reconciliation are tested as a full path.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery progress, gaps, validation, divergence and residual unknowns are visible.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Provides a coherent internal recovery point without stopping the system where assumptions permit.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Storage/stream/workflow runtime and recovery operator.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Internal consistency does not guarantee external world consistency
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From global coordinated checkpoints to asynchronous barriers, incremental snapshots and log/snapshot hybrids.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Snapshot identifies membership/configuration, state versions, channel/log positions and excluded external effects.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Having periodic snapshots is not a consistent recovery cut.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can large geo-distributed snapshots remain cheap without weakening recovery semantics?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Can restored local checkpoints and in-flight messages form a state that never existed?
Which external effects are outside the snapshot?

PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any availability, durability, disaster recovery or rollback claim with material consequence.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Low-consequence disposable state that can be regenerated and whose loss is explicitly accepted.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Immutable backups/logs, independent access, compatible tooling, capacity, validation oracle, runbook and ownership.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Process/storage crash, partition, inconsistent checkpoint, orphan message/work, log gap, corruption, stale failover authority and external-state divergence.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Recovery point/time objectives are evidence-backed, not inferred from backup existence.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: The recovery line is internally consistent and reconciled with effects outside the log/transaction boundary.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Restored configuration, ownership generation and membership are current; old writers are fenced.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Replay/redelivery uses original identities and does not duplicate unclosed effects.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Snapshots, logs, backups, restore tooling, capacity and reconciliation are tested as a full path.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery progress, gaps, validation, divergence and residual unknowns are visible.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Converts recovery design into current empirical evidence and exposes hidden dependencies before crisis.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Data owner, operator, incident commander and assurance reviewer.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Passing one scenario does not cover all common modes
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From backup existence checks to end-to-end restore, failover, reconciliation and return-to-service exercises.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Recovery evidence includes current artefact identity, measured RPO/RTO, authority fencing, external reconciliation and unresolved residuals.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A backup job marked successful is not a restore path.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.

Did the test include replay, catch-up, authority, external reconciliation and return to service?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Schema, wire protocol and event evolution under mixed versions
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Database schema evolution, protocol negotiation, online upgrades and event-log replay.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Old and new producers, consumers, stored events and replicas must interoperate during rollout, rollback and replay.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Rolling upgrades create a mixed-version distributed system even when every binary is individually healthy.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Components observe incompatible schemas/protocols at different times and old events outlive the code that wrote them.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Decode failure, silent field loss, semantic reinterpretation, replay breakage and rollback impossibility.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Version schemas/protocols; define backward/forward compatibility; use additive/staged changes; negotiate capabilities; retain old-reader/writer tests and migration/rollback plan.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Rolling deployment, long-lived event/log data, external clients, multiple regions or replayable workflow history.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Atomic offline upgrade of one local process/store with no concurrent old reader/writer and acceptable downtime.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Version inventory, compatibility matrix, contract tests using real historical data, field semantics and rollback/downgrade policy.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Mixed versions, incompatible wire/schema changes, stale configuration, control-plane/data-plane skew and rollback incompatibility.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Propagation is asynchronous; 'flag set' or 'deployment complete' is not proof every component observed it.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Readers/writers define compatibility across old/new schemas and replayed historical events.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Current configuration/version authority and staged rollout state are reconstructable.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Messages/events are versioned and unknown fields/semantics handled deliberately.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Rollback and replay paths are compatible with new writes; downgrade limits are explicit.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Version distribution, configuration convergence and compatibility errors are visible.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Allows continuous change without turning version skew into hidden partial failure.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Service/API owner, data platform, deployer, client and recovery operator.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Additive change is not always possible
Syntactic compatibility can hide semantic incompatibility
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From stop-the-world migration to staged expand/migrate/contract, capability negotiation and replay-aware versioning.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Every live old/new reader, writer, replica and history has a tested compatibility path or an explicit cutover barrier.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: 'Rolling deployment succeeded' is not protocol compatibility.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should very long-lived event histories be retired without retaining every old semantic forever?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Can every old/new producer, consumer and stored event interoperate during rollout and rollback?
Does syntactic compatibility preserve field meaning and invariants?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Current dependency topology and end-to-end readiness
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Distributed monitoring, service-dependency practice and outages where local health diverged from usable service.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: A component is ready only for a declared effect path, with current dependencies, capacity and authority—not because its process answers.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Health endpoint is green while database, DNS, queue, credential, control plane or downstream effect path is stale/unusable.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Dependencies fail independently and topology changes dynamically; local checks cover only one process.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Traffic sent to unusable instances, false completion, cascading retries and delayed diagnosis.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Discover/version topology; separate liveness/readiness; exercise synthetic end-to-end paths; check dependency currentness/capacity and effect boundary; degrade by capability.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Service depends on remote components or dynamic routing/ownership.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Standalone local process with no remote effect path, where process liveness is the whole service.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Current topology, dependency contracts, credentials/routing, representative probes, consequence-safe synthetic operations and freshness bounds.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Missing spans/logs, sampling bias, clock skew, telemetry delay/outage, cardinality loss, stale topology and observer effects.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Telemetry has acquisition/ingestion delay and clock uncertainty; currentness is bounded or marked unknown.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Telemetry consistency does not imply application-state consistency.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Source identity, configuration and topology provenance accompany observations.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Trace context/correlation may be dropped, duplicated or sampled.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Evidence survives or is intentionally preserved through failure and recovery.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Coverage, sampling, missingness and uncertainty are first-class data.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Routes and declares service based on usable capabilities rather than process existence.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Load balancer, orchestrator, operator and calling service.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: End-to-end probes cost capacity and can mutate data
No finite probe covers all paths
Dependency awareness can create tight coupling
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From ping/process checks to capability-specific readiness, topology reconstruction and black-box effect tests.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Readiness states the exact effect path and evidence age; green does not imply every dependency or operation is healthy.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A `/health` 200 response is not service readiness.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.

PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Local deterministic operation with direct authoritative state inspection.

Metric aggregate hides one unsafe operation

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Causal trace reconstruction and event provenance
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Logical clocks, distributed snapshots, X-Trace/Dapper and trace-context standards.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Reconstruct enough causal and authority provenance to explain an operation across components, not merely correlate similar timestamps.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Logs share IDs/times but lack parentage, message/effect identity, configuration and authority generation.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Events are reordered, sampled and emitted by processes with skewed clocks and changing topology.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Incorrect root-cause order, inability to link retries/effects, and false claim that correlation proves causation.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Propagate trace and operation identity, parent/links, config/term/version and event source; preserve causal edges; annotate gaps and sampled branches.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Debugging, audit, recovery or completion requires cross-component reconstruction.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: One local process with deterministic logs and no remote effects.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable identity, context propagation, causal model, clock uncertainty, sampling metadata, source provenance and retention.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Missing spans/logs, sampling bias, clock skew, telemetry delay/outage, cardinality loss, stale topology and observer effects.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Telemetry has acquisition/ingestion delay and clock uncertainty; currentness is bounded or marked unknown.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Telemetry consistency does not imply application-state consistency.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Source identity, configuration and topology provenance accompany observations.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Trace context/correlation may be dropped, duplicated or sampled.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Evidence survives or is intentionally preserved through failure and recovery.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Coverage, sampling, missingness and uncertainty are first-class data.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Improves fault discrimination and links retries, authority changes and effects without inventing total order.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Debugger, incident investigator, recovery planner and auditor.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Causal provenance cannot include unobserved physical events automatically
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From timestamped logs to explicit parent/link graphs, operation/effect identity and authority/configuration provenance.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Reconstruction distinguishes known causal edges, concurrent events, inferred links and missing evidence.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Correlation IDs plus sorted timestamps are not causal proof.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can provenance cross organisations while respecting privacy and trust boundaries?

Where are trace gaps or inferred—not observed—edges recorded?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Hypothesis-bound fault injection and recovery challenge
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Software fault injection, production failure testing and chaos-engineering practice.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Empirically challenge a specific current failure/recovery claim under bounded, observable conditions.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Failure assumptions and runbooks remain untested, or chaos exercises become repetitive spectacle without decision consequence.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Real distributed failures depend on timing, topology, load, persistence and recovery interaction that unit tests miss.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Unknown failover/recovery behaviour, false confidence and discovery of critical coupling only during outage.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: State hypothesis/invariant; choose representative fault schedule/load; bound blast radius; predeclare evidence/stop conditions; test recovery/reconciliation; record decision.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Material claim about tolerance, failover, retry, restore, overload or state integrity whose assumptions can be safely challenged.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Static analysis/model checking/unit/integration test when the claim does not require distributed runtime failure; low-consequence system with no material uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Representative environment/configuration, observability, rollback, safety authority, current topology, consequence assessment and independent expected result.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Unexercised failure assumptions, non-representative injections, uncontrolled blast radius, missing observability and untested recovery.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Injection timing/order and stop conditions are part of the experiment.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: The tested invariant/postcondition is explicit; steady-state proxy alone is insufficient.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Experiment authority, scope and rollback are bounded.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Injected faults include loss, delay, duplicate/reorder where relevant.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: The experiment tests recovery and post-recovery reconciliation, not merely failure onset.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Predeclared evidence and abort conditions must be available.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Provides current empirical evidence and discovers integration faults outside formal or design models.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System owner, operator, assurance reviewer and incident-response planner.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Staging may not reproduce common modes
Evidence for broad effectiveness remains heterogeneous
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From random process killing to hypothesis-, invariant-, load-, recovery- and decision-bound experiments plus systematic schedule generation.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A bounded experiment challenges one explicit claim and its recovery path; pass/fail changes evidence or action.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: 'Run chaos experiments' is not a general property.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can chaos-engineering benefit be measured independently of adoption theatre and reporting bias?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What exact failure/recovery claim does the experiment challenge?
Does it test the current configuration, load, external effects and post-recovery reconciliation?
