PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Distribution requires a named consumer and retains a cheap local path
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Repeated contrast between local atomicity and the costs introduced by RPC, partial failure, microservices and distributed transactions.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Distribute only for a concrete need—failure independence, latency locality, scale, ownership/autonomy or separate lifecycle—and preserve the simpler non-trigger.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Remote boundaries are introduced because the architecture is fashionable rather than because they serve a requirement.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Every unnecessary boundary adds delay, unknown outcomes, version skew, partial failure, observability and recovery state.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Overengineering small/local problems and making correctness depend on infrastructure with no consumer.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Name the consumer, quantify its need, compare local/single-owner alternative, and keep distribution out of paths where it adds no payoff.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Independent scaling, fault containment, geographic latency, ownership/autonomy or deployment lifecycle demonstrably outweighs coordination cost.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Co-locate code/state, use in-process calls and local transactions, or one durable owner.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Workload/consequence evidence, ownership model, availability/latency target and explicit cost/complexity comparison.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Ceremonial architecture can introduce partial failure, coordination debt and unowned recovery without a protected consumer.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: No general timing model; the claim fails because a named artefact is substituted for an engineering property.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: No guarantee follows from branding alone.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: No authority follows from deployment labels alone.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: No delivery/effect semantics follow from tooling labels alone.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery evidence follows from having a component installed.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Dashboards and green checks are proxies unless tied to a claim.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Preserves engineering value while stripping cloud-native fashion and accidental distribution.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, product owner, operations and the team bearing lifecycle cost.
KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Organisational boundary mistaken for runtime boundary
Remote API hides shared database/common mode
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Local design may create migration cost
No universal threshold separates local from distributed
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From default networked decomposition to deliberate distribution with explicit trigger and reversible cheap path.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Every remote boundary names the property it buys, the assumptions it creates and the condition for collapsing it.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Microservices, queues, service mesh or consensus are not maturity indicators.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can teams preserve future optionality without paying distributed-system cost prematurely?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What concrete scale, latency, autonomy, lifecycle or failure-independence consumer justifies each remote boundary?
Could the same invariant or workflow be local without losing that consumer?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Retire distributed machinery when its coordination consumer disappears
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Operational experience with long-lived middleware, consensus, queues and service decompositions.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Coordination mechanisms are contingent means, not permanent institutions.

PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Obsolete machinery continues generating partial failure, upgrade, recovery and observability burden.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Ceremonial complexity, stale authority paths, unowned retries/backlogs and hidden single points of failure.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Periodically restate consumer and trigger; measure use; plan drain/migration; preserve evidence and rollback; collapse to local/simple path when justified.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Mechanism has no current decision, invariant, workload or failure-domain consumer.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Keep mechanism only when removal would reintroduce a demonstrated failure or violate a current requirement.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Usage/dependency inventory, migration/replay plan, retained data/identity semantics and safe decommission evidence.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Ceremonial architecture can introduce partial failure, coordination debt and unowned recovery without a protected consumer.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: No general timing model; the claim fails because a named artefact is substituted for an engineering property.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: No guarantee follows from branding alone.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: No authority follows from deployment labels alone.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: No delivery/effect semantics follow from tooling labels alone.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery evidence follows from having a component installed.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Dashboards and green checks are proxies unless tied to a claim.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents coordination debt from becoming an irreversible part of the system.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architecture owner, platform owner and operational teams.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Benefits are hard to quantify before removal
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From infrastructure accumulation to lifecycle ownership with explicit retirement conditions and evidence.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Each distributed mechanism has entry, operation and exit criteria; decommission preserves state and effect semantics.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: 'Standard platform component' is not a permanent justification.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Which current invariant or consumer still requires this mechanism?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Microservices automatically improve resilience
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Service-oriented and microservice architecture advocacy, contradicted by distributed coordination and integrity evidence.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Decompose into independently deployable services and infer resilience from separation.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Deployment boundaries are mistaken for independent failure domains and semantic isolation.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Calls, data and retries cross more failure boundaries while dependencies and shared control planes remain coupled.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: This candidate prevents no general failure; it can create coordination debt unless real isolation/ownership is established.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: NO_GENERAL_PROPERTY. Evaluate each boundary for independent failure/deployment/ownership benefit, data integrity, retries, capacity and recovery.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Retain a service boundary only when it creates a real independently operable/failing/owned capability.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Modular monolith, local module or co-located state when independent runtime failure is unnecessary.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Independent data/authority, API semantics, capacity/isolation, end-to-end observability and recovery ownership.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Ceremonial architecture can introduce partial failure, coordination debt and unowned recovery without a protected consumer.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: No general timing model; the claim fails because a named artefact is substituted for an engineering property.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: No guarantee follows from branding alone.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: No authority follows from deployment labels alone.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: No delivery/effect semantics follow from tooling labels alone.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery evidence follows from having a component installed.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Dashboards and green checks are proxies unless tied to a claim.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Rejecting the automatic claim avoids architecture-by-brand while preserving useful service boundaries.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, service owner and operations.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Microservices can genuinely improve autonomy and fault containment
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From decomposition as default modernity to boundary-by-boundary evaluation and selective recombination.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A service boundary is justified by a named lifecycle, ownership, scale or failure-containment property and bears its distributed obligations.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The rejected proposition is itself a cloud-native caricature.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Microservices can deliver real independent deployment and scaling; the rejected element is the automatic, general resilience inference.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which comparative empirical designs can isolate architecture shape from organisational maturity and workload?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Which service boundaries correspond to independent failure, scale, ownership or deployment consumers?
Which merely add remote coordination and data-integrity burden?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Byzantine/adversarial fault tolerance only under an explicit adversarial model
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Byzantine agreement and practical Byzantine state-machine replication.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Replicate/agree despite arbitrary or malicious replica behaviour under authentication and threshold assumptions.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Crash-fault systems are described with Byzantine terminology without modelling compromised replicas, identities, cryptographic trust or correlated implementation faults.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Participants can send conflicting, malformed or strategically adversarial messages rather than merely stop.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Agreement/safety loss caused by up to the modelled number of arbitrary faulty participants.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Use authenticated BFT protocol, 3f+1-style or protocol-specific threshold, independent administrative/failure domains, key/identity governance and deterministic validation.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Actual threat model includes mutually distrustful or compromise-prone participants and the cost is justified.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Crash-fault consensus, single authority, audited replication or simpler integrity checks when adversarial participants are not a credible failure.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Adversary/corruption model, authentication, identity/key lifecycle, independence, quorum threshold, denial-of-service/liveness assumptions and implementation assurance.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Domain-specific crash, omission, arbitrary/value, model, scheduling and external-service failures.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Domain workload and latency model must be stated.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Domain semantic validity remains separate from replicated agreement or durable execution.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Distributed AI and agentic systems as a bounded domain translation
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Multi-agent planning, agent workflows, tool-calling systems and recent attempts to apply sagas, validation and chaos testing.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Treat agents/models/tools as independently failing distributed actors with durable context, operation identity, validation and effect reconciliation.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Probabilistic outputs, tool calls and context versions add semantic/value failure beyond crash/omission while familiar retry and workflow risks remain.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Agents, models, retrieval stores and tools can omit, duplicate, delay, hallucinate or semantically conflict while external effects persist.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Duplicate tools/effects, stale context, unvalidated plan execution, lost workflow state and false completion.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Durable workflow state, versioned context/model/tool provenance, constrained authority, semantic validation, idempotent/fenced tool effects, compensation and targeted fault injection.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Autonomous or multi-agent system coordinates persistent work or external effects across independently failing services.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: One model call with human review and no durable/external effect; deterministic local program where suitable.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Agent/task identity, model/prompt/tool versions, validator authority, external effect closure, human escalation and privacy/security constraints.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Domain-specific crash, omission, arbitrary/value, model, scheduling and external-service failures.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: Domain workload and latency model must be stated.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Domain semantic validity remains separate from replicated agreement or durable execution.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Agent/service/model/tool authority and version are explicit.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: Calls can be duplicated, omitted, delayed or return malformed/semantically invalid values.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: State/context, tool effects and human escalation are durable and reconcilable.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Prompt/model/tool version, causal provenance and validation evidence are captured within privacy/security limits.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Transfers proven distributed-state disciplines while acknowledging probabilistic semantic uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Agent-platform owner, workflow designer, tool/effect owner and human supervisor.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Evidence is very recent and mostly prototypes/preprints
Anthropomorphic 'agent' framing can obscure ordinary workflow design
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Current translation is moving from chat/session memory to durable, validated, transaction-like agent workflows and fault injection.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Provisional: agentic execution is governed as a durable distributed workflow, but probabilistic semantic validity is not promoted to a solved systems property.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: 'Multi-agent' does not imply distributed-systems maturity.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: Whether agent-specific reliability mechanisms form genuinely new general properties remains unresolved.
Operational field evidence and independent replication are sparse.
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Which agent/tool effects can duplicate or remain unknown after retry?
What validates semantic correctness independently of the agent reporting success?
Can model/prompt/context versions reproduce or explain an action?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Default global consensus or coordination for all distributed state
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Consensus folklore and overgeneralisation from strong consistency/transactions.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Put every state transition through one global order or distributed lock because distribution exists.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Coordination is used without a non-confluent invariant or current-authority consumer.
PROPERTIES.DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE: Global quorum/leader becomes latency, availability and throughput dependency; failure domain expands.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: No general failure is prevented when operations commute, partition safely, tolerate staleness or can be locally owned.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: NO_GENERAL_PROPERTY. Start with P14/P45; use P16 for safe autonomy and P15 only for the minimal non-confluent invariant.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Strong coordination triggers only for an explicit invariant/current authority that cannot be preserved by local ownership, partitioning, commutativity, escrow or compensation.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Local transaction, single writer, CRDT/invariant-confluent operation, partitioned ownership or asynchronous durable handoff.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Invariant analysis, operation algebra, failure/latency target, membership and recovery evidence.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODEL: Ceremonial architecture can introduce partial failure, coordination debt and unowned recovery without a protected consumer.
PROPERTIES.TIMING_MODEL: No general timing model; the claim fails because a named artefact is substituted for an engineering property.
PROPERTIES.CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: No guarantee follows from branding alone.
PROPERTIES.MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: No authority follows from deployment labels alone.
PROPERTIES.DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS: No delivery/effect semantics follow from tooling labels alone.
PROPERTIES.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery evidence follows from having a component installed.
PROPERTIES.OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Dashboards and green checks are proxies unless tied to a claim.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Avoids global bottlenecks and availability loss while retaining coordination where it actually buys correctness.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Application/data architect and invariant owner.
IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Simplicity of one order can outweigh cost at modest scale
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From one-size-fits-all strong ordering to invariant-scoped coordination and hybrid systems.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Coordinate only the state/effect closure whose independent execution would violate the named invariant.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: 'Distributed means consensus' is the rejected caricature.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Global ordering can be the simplest correct choice at modest scale when a central invariant dominates; the rejected element is defaulting without that consumer.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can teams reliably discover hidden non-confluent invariants before removing coordination?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Which invariant requires a global order?
Could local ownership, commutativity, partitioning, escrow or compensation preserve it more cheaply?
